items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: influencing Alvin Batiste, Ellis Marsalis, Ed Blackwell and all these other people.

ctx.x: And actually that’s really interesting because, well a lot of people, and hopefully you’ll get a chance to introduce, well interview, Harold Batiste. I don’t know if you’re familiar with Harold Batiste. But Harold was sort of like the person who was teaching Ellis and Nat Perrillat and all these other people tunes that Charlie Parker was writing. I mean he was a person transcribing in New Orleans and well this is what Bird played and this is the tune that he played and this is my tune and this is how this goes.…

influencing Alvin Batiste, Ellis Marsalis, Ed Blackwell and all these other people. And it’s really interesting because you just never know, you know, who’s going to be the person with the invisible hand behind the scene telling people well this is the music, this is the new thing, this is what’s going on. It’s really interesting.
Do you have a description of what it is you’re trying to do with your music?
